title: SDK Explorer: incremental onramp + telemetry quickstart (scratchpad)
content:
Purpose:
- Lightweight, incremental quickstart for internal SDK adopters who want fast feedback on telemetry and failure modes.
- Focus: get a dev to a working sample app + meaningful telemetry within 15–25 minutes.

Audience:
- SDK integrators, solutions engineers, and PMs running early pilots.
- New hires who need a compact, instrumented example to learn telemetry contracts.

Goals (MVP):
1) A single repo sample app that: authenticates, sends text generation requests, streams responses, and records telemetry events defined below.
2) A minimal CLI flow (bootstrap -> run -> inspect) so devs can replicate telemetry locally.
3) A readable telemetry contract (event names + required fields) inlined in the quickstart.
4) Short troubleshooting notes for 5 common failure modes.

Success metrics (first 90 days):
- 75% of pilot devs complete the quickstart within 25 min (user testing).
- Telemetry events show ingestion for 90% of executed sample requests in staging.
- Two integrations open PRs referencing the example repo.

Constraints / non-goals:
- Not targeting heavy production architecture (no infra-as-code, no k8s manifests).
- Not a full SDK API reference — this is a practical runloop + telemetry primer.

Quickstart sketch (15–25 minutes):
0) Prereqs (2 min):
- node >=18 or python3.11 installed
- yarn or npm (for web sample) / pip for python sample
- REDWOOD_API_KEY set in env (dev key from ./secrets/dev-keys)

1) Clone & bootstrap (3 min):
- git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/sdk-explorer.git && cd sdk-explorer/samples/quick-telemetry
- ./bootstrap.sh  # creates .env, installs deps, starts local stub if needed

Notes: bootstrap.sh should detect local-mode and prompt: "Start local stub (y/n)?" — default yes for first-time users.

2) Run the sample app (5 min):
- node ./index.js  # interactive prompt that hits the Redwood text-gen API and streams tokens
- python serve_sample.py  # alternative python path

Expected output: streaming tokens printed to terminal, plus a JSON line that is a telemetry event sent to staging endpoint.

3) Inspect telemetry (5 min):
- open http://localhost:8428/telemetry (simple flyway UI) OR 
- tail ./logs/telemetry.log to see parsed events

Telemetry contract (inline / canonical):
- event: sdk.request.start
  - required: request_id, sdk_version, sample_app, user_hash, timestamp, model_name, route
- event: sdk.request.chunk
  - required: request_id, chunk_index, chunk_len, cumulative_tokens, timestamp
- event: sdk.request.complete
  - required: request_id, status (ok|partial|error), total_tokens, latency_ms, timestamp, cost_usd_estimate
- event: sdk.error.rate_limit
  - required: request_id, status_code, retry_after, route, timestamp
- event: sdk.telemetry.heartbeat
  - required: sdk_version, sample_app, uptime_s, queued_requests_count, timestamp

Contract notes: keep payloads shallow; prefer consistent primitives (strings, ints, floats). No nested objects beyond a small metadata map (max 3 keys).

Sample telemetry example (one-line JSON):
{"event":"sdk.request.start","request_id":"r-0a1b2c","sdk_version":"0.9.1-explorer","sample_app":"quick-telemetry","user_hash":"u-42","timestamp":"2025-02-06T16:02:08Z","model_name":"rw-v1-small","route":"/v1/generate"}

Minimum SDK behavior tested in quickstart:
- handle 429 -> backoff 2s -> retry x2 then surface sdk.error.rate_limit
- stream partial responses and emit sdk.request.chunk for each chunk
- compute naive cost estimate per-token and include in sdk.request.complete
- attach sdk_version and sample_app labels to all telemetry

Developer-facing checklist (for docs page):
- [ ] One-liner: what this quickstart teaches
- [ ] Prereqs and quick bootstrap command
- [ ] Minimal run command for both node & python
- [ ] Telemetry viewing instructions (local + staging)
- [ ] Top 5 troubleshooting items (below)
- [ ] Link to full telemetry spec (Confluence) and SDK repo

Top 5 troubleshooting (concise):
1) No streaming output: check REDWOOD_API_KEY, confirm sample is hitting correct route (env uses STAGING by default).
2) Telemetry not showing: ensure local telemetry sink started via ./bootstrap.sh; check TELEMETRY_ENDPOINT in .env.
3) 429s repeatedly: confirm dev key quota; switch to a lower-rate sample loop (use --rate-limit flag).
4) Error: missing request_id in logs: upgrade quick-telemetry to sdk v0.9.1-explorer or set REQUEST_ID env override.
5) Windows line-endings break bootstrap.sh: run bash in WSL or use bootstrap.ps1 for PowerShell.

Rollout plan (phased):
- Week 0–1: internal smoke test with 3 SEs + 2 engs, iterate bootstrap UX and clearer error copy.
- Week 2: publish to internal GH org, add README and short Loom recording (2–3 min).
- Week 3–4: enable staging telemetry ingestion and measure success metrics; adjust contract if events miss required fields.
- Month 2: promote sample to public quickstarts if no major contract churn.

Open questions / notes-to-self:
- Do we want to include a browser-based variant that uses the streaming SSE path? pros: easier demo; cons: CORS + token leakage educational risk.
- Should the sample compute cost using per-model rates or mock rates? Mock rates avoid frequent model catalog churn.
- How opinionated should bootstrap.sh be about local stubs vs staging?  (default local-first feels friendlier)
- Add a small e2e test that validates telemetry fields emitted by the sample during CI.

Follow-ups / next steps (priority ordered):
1) Jonah: prototype bootstrap.sh prompts and local telemetry sink (WIP PR linked above).
2) Priya: draft README + two short Loom clips (bootstrap + telemetry inspect).
3) Maya: implement a tiny health-check that asserts sdk.request.start & sdk.request.complete emitted for each run (CI script).

Related tickets & references:
- PLATFORM-2193: telemetry contract review (owner: infra-telemetry team)
- SDK-EXPLORER PR 142: bootstrap.sh + sample server changes (link above)
- CONFLUENCE-DEVEXP-ONRAMP: longer form spec + rollout notes

Quick copy for README top (first 2 lines):
"A 15-minute instrumented SDK quickstart that teaches streaming, retries, and telemetry. Start local, run a sample, inspect events."

TODO (short list):
- [ ] finalize telemetry event names with infra team
- [ ] add python CLI entrypoint and example flags (--rate-limit, --local-stub)
- [ ] smoke-test on Windows + Mac M1 in next round
- [ ] tiny CI check to assert telemetry schema fields present

If you're reading this and want to help: ping me (maya@redwood.ai) in #devexp or add comments to PR 142.

-- end of scratchpad --
